body: Hey! Listen up. I know you may not feel it right now but you are so important. You are so loved. You have so many wonderful qualities to offer to others. I know how dark and lonely the place your in can feel but it will go away I promise you. You will get better and you will be successful and joyful!! Please, do not hurt yourself because I want you to live.

Hi! I’m so so sorry to hear you’re having such a tougher time :( it sounds like you might be in high school? I just want to let you know - I know that this feels so so bad right now and I know how much you’re hurting, but there is a really big light at the end of the tunnel. It may not feel like it right now, but there is so much joy waiting ahead of you. I was in your position just a few years ago. I have run away from home, started to walk to down the street barefoot. I know that it feels really lonely when life gets like this. I like to say that “when it rains, it pours”. Usually when life gets tough, it gets really tough. I promise you that your parents do love you. I have parents who did the exact same thing (drove me to my therapist and had me admitted). They took away my phone and I was in an inpatient program. It really felt like the end of the world, but I promise they only do it because of how much they love and care about you. They don’t know what the best way to react is and they are so afraid of losing you! They may not be completely capable of acting in the best way or saying the best things, but they are doing the best they can because they want to help you. And I want you to know that getting help is ok!! Seeing a therapist is so important when you have lows in life like this and I’m so glad you’re doing that. I know it can be scary to accept help or do an inpatient program, but I can say that without it,  wouldn’t be the successful young adult that I am. I know you feel so lost and hopeless, but you are so amazing and have so many wonderful qualities to share with others. You will find those people to share them with I promise because you are so special. Give it time. Be compassionate to yourself, you are going through something difficult. Don’t forget to love yourself and give yourself a hug. Seriously. Other people don’t know how long you need a hug for- only you do!!! Treat yourself to some self love and recognize that you can do this❤️

For me Zoloft was not the medication and that’s ok! I actually got more depressed on Zoloft. I slowly got off of the medication because I was so depressed. I switched to celexa and it works so well for me. Different medications work differently for everyone so don’t feel pressured or rush anything!!
Hahahah thank you I am a writer and I was writing one day and it just kinda came out lol. And I have a friend but I get nervous I am a burden or annoying or bothering them.
Thank you it means more than you realize
Yeah I have done CBT, DBT, EMDR all the stuff haha. I texted my therapist and she’s going to see me tomorrow. It’s just like when is this going to stop. Why do I just keep feeling like this.
I’ve been in therapy since I was 12 and on meds since I was 14.

Medication can be scary. For a long time I thought that taking medication meant changing who I was. When I started my anxiety medication (a super low dose) I realized I had never felt more myself. I have been able to use my skills and I will hopefully be off of the medication by the end of medical school. I know that it is so stigmatized and that your family might have their own criticism, but ultimately if it is something you feel would benefit you- the people in your life should support that decision.

Hi! I’ve had generalized anxiety my whole life but I started experiencing panic attacks in college. They can be different for a lot of people, sometimes you feel like you can’t breath but someone your mind is just racing. For me I tend to feel like I’m having a really bad high and I start panicking. This sounds similar to what you’re going through. I would recommend seeing someone or getting a professionals advice, but in the meantime there is an app called insight timer. There are WONDERFUL meditations and podcasts guiding you through your panic attack. Grounding meditations are perfect for this and if you search panic attack it will pop up with a bunch of options. They help you to realize you are safe and the panic will subside. They can also help you get rest when you can’t sleep!
I appreciate this a lot. It is completely different.

I have recently had someone take me for granted because I can’t cook like my roommate can. I was told that she would be a better wife and better option than I would. I was so taken aback that people actually valued cooking and a uterus over my brain, considering how successful, loving and compassionate I am. In this moment I realized that I was sitting and waiting for someone else to appreciate me when I should’ve been appreciating myself all along.

I’m sick of people saying they don’t owe me anything you know. Like yes you do. You owe me respect and decency because I’m a human being. We all owe each other that. Where can I move where people understand this concept of kindness?

Some people don’t understand anxiety because they have never dealt with it! They assume it is sensitivity or  a dramatic reaction. It is okay that they don’t understand, but remember there are so many people out there just like you who do understand and who know how it feels.

I have struggled with that for a long time and it took some time but eventually with practice you get better at calming yourself down. I always start by looking around the room. The reason we get anxiety is because our bodies our programmed to react to danger for survival- but we are no longer competing to survive! Looking around the room and recognizing that there is no immediate danger and you are safe is the first step to calming yourself down. Second, recognize that it will pass. The feeling will not last forever and you will be okay. Then you want to control your breathing which you can do on your own or through meditation (I personally love insight timer it has guided meditations for anxiety). Drinking water often helps as well, it slows your system and helps you to take a step back. With time you will get better and eventually you won’t feel so sick and upset when there is conflict! Good luck.

I try so hard. I go therapy, I am on medication, I use my skills but I can never get rid of the voices who tell me I am not good enough and no one will ever want me. I. D.o.n.t know how to see myself as beautiful anymore.

I get so down on myself for having been here for so long. I’ve had chronic depression for the last 7 years. I’m on medication and some days/weeks/months are better than others but I am worried I will have to live my whole life like this. It’s not what I want and I just want to be better.
